StackType.rationale: PowerStackType.Counter. The sim has no StackType concept; Power.on_stack adds unconditionally, which is what PowerCmd.ModifyAmount does (PowerCmd.cs:236 -- no StackType branch). Third-file citations, not hashed here.

ShouldPowerBeRemovedAfterOwnerDeath.rationale: `=> false`. C# strips a dead creature's powers at CreatureCmd.cs:533; the sim never removes powers on death, so `false` is its universal behaviour and this override is satisfied for free. The inverse -- the C# default is `true` and the sim strips nothing -- is the engine-wide absence reported in content-power-report-b.md section 3c. ENGINE-LEVEL SIBLING (added 2026-07-26): the INVERSE finding -- that C#'s DEFAULT is `true` so every power WITHOUT this override should be stripped on its owner's death and in the sim none is -- now carries a verdict of its own at audit/records/seam/creature_card_cmds.json step 8b (`gap`, LIVE, executed on the Decimillipede). It used to exist only as prose in content-power-report-b.md section 3c. This entry stays `faithful` because the override asks for exactly the behaviour the sim gives for free; the engine-wide absence is step 8b's, not this unit's.

ShouldCreatureBeRemovedFromCombatAfterDe.maps_to: hooks.py:603 -- NOT implemented by this power
ShouldCreatureBeRemovedFromCombatAfterDe.issue: `=> creature != base.Owner`, i.e. the Test Subject's corpse stays in combat. The sim has the hook (hooks.py:603, consumed at cmds.py:102-104) and this power does not use it -- AdaptablePower on the same creature prevents the death instead (audit/records/power/adaptable.json), so the phase transition works by a different route. Same unused-hook finding as adaptable's and illusion's; folded into that mechanism.

AfterAttack.issue: WRONG HOOK, and the sim HAS the right one and does not use it. C#'s `AfterAttack(choiceContext, AttackCommand command)` fires ONCE per attack command, after every hit of every target, and is handed the whole `command.Results` (a List<List<DamageResult>>) so it can count hits and act once. The sim ports it onto `on_damage_received` (cmds.py:122), which fires PER HIT and inside the damage pipeline. `hooks.py:344` (before_attack) and `hooks.py:361` (after_attack) both exist -- the main report records them as used by Vigor and Gigantification -- so this is an unused-slot omission, not an absence. Same defect as curl_up's and skittish's (main report section 4 items 5 and 14). Two standing consequences: the KILLING-BLOW guard (cmds.py:121 skips the victim's on_damage_received on a kill, where C#'s AfterAttack is not guarded at all), and effects granted inline being visible to LATER HITS OF THE SAME attack. Third-file citations, not hashed here. Here the Wound COUNT works out the same -- C# adds `base.Amount * num` Wounds once where num is the number of connecting hits (PainfulStabsPower.cs:60-62) and the sim adds `self.amount` per connecting hit (powers.py:3408-3409) -- so the arithmetic is equivalent and the divergences are the two standing ones. (a) KILLING BLOW: this power's target is the PLAYER, so on a lethal hit cmds.py:121 suppresses the sim's on_damage_received and the game's AfterAttack still adds the Wounds. That is not purely academic -- with the ported Lizard Tail preventing the death, cmds.py:112 floors the player at 1 HP and `target.is_dead` is then False, so the sim DOES fire; the two models therefore agree on the prevented-death path and disagree on the real-death path, which is the inverse of damage_pipeline gap G4's shape. (b) TIMING: Wounds arriving in the discard mid-attack rather than after it, which nothing currently reads. Also faithful for the record: C# adds to `PileType.Discard` and the sim uses `CardPileCmd.add_to_discard` -- the pile is right, which matters because Wounds in the DRAW pile would be a different card. Third-file citations, not hashed here.

guards.rationale: `command.Attacker != base.Owner`, `command.TargetSide == base.Owner.Side`, `!command.DamageProps.IsPoweredAttack()` map to powers.py:3400-3405's `dealer is self.owner and target.side == "player" and amount > 0 and is_powered_attack(props)`. The props test reads `props` directly, which is the correct form (contrast SlowPower's card-based test).
The sim's per-hit `amount > 0` is the same predicate evaluated per hit; with the count equivalence above the totals agree.
